source.title: Statistical and Privacy Guarantees for Deep M-Regression via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics
source.authors: Ye-Heng Ge; Jian Huang; Shu-Yuan Wu

record.tranche_reason: Reports new results on how injected SGLD noise relates to predictive performance in regression and classification. This extends generalization evidence to SGLD and these tasks, but does not test the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study varies injected Gaussian noise and reports predictive test metrics. Its results concern noise effects, a condition not directly covered by V1–V8; theoretical bounds are not empirical results about those versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests how injected SGLD noise affects prediction and privacy, but none of V1–V8. Its discussion of wide valleys does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' empirical conclusion: predictive performance changes modestly across the reported moderate-noise real-data settings while reported asymptotic GDP parameters decrease. Their broader conclusion also includes conditional optimal regression rates up to logarithmic factors and finite-sample f-DP guarantees; the statistical rates require controlled trajectory complexity and optimization error.
record.recipe_differences: Studies injected Gaussian noise in SGLD for regression and classification, comparing noise levels rather than testing random-label memorization, width, architecture comparisons, optimizer families, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictive metrics vary with injected-noise level; the largest tested noise level worsened reported test loss in the simulation settings described.

fits_no_version.finding: On ACTG-175, moderate injected noise changes mean test RMSE from 0.7491 to 0.7464 or 0.7466. On MNIST, it changes mean accuracy from 97.518% to 97.303% or 97.123%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Moderate SGLD noise can accompany small improvements or declines in held-out performance, depending on the task and noise level.

record.problems: The study does not test the listed versions. Empirical evaluations are limited to specified simulated and real-data settings; ACTG-175 and MNIST results use 20 replications, and exact uncertainty values are not stated in the text for the reported comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.1 reports figure-based toy sparse linear regression results for SCAD and LASSO, but these are not neural networks. Section 4.2 describes six quantile-regression settings: the text gives only qualitative patterns and points to figure-only values, so these were not added as separate rows. Section 4.3 reports figure-based results for three sample sizes at γ⁻¹ = 10⁻⁴ and 5 × 10⁻⁴; the text provides only the latter's qualitative threshold (>2.2), and these rows were omitted to prioritize the directly stated MNIST and ACTG values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization under matched recipes, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and effects of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The regression and CNN experiments use different tasks and cannot establish V3. Added Gaussian noise is not dropout, adaptive optimization, or a batch-size intervention. The simulation findings omitted from the rows are declared in rows_left_out and do not bear on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; chance accuracy with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning or weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
